name: Tarsal-carpal coalition syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and radiological diagnostic criteria for tarsal-carpal coalition syndrome

criteria.description: Radiographic or CT evidence of coalition between tarsal and carpal bones
Presence of congenital malformations of hands and feet including limited joint mobility
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Exclusion of other syndromes with similar presentations such as symphalangism or multiple synostoses syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of radiographic evidence of tarsal-carpal coalition plus congenital malformations of hands and feet with exclusion of other syndromes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

imaging: X-ray demonstrating fusion of tarsal and carpal bones
CT scan confirming extent of coalition and bony bridging
other: Physical examination revealing limited joint mobility and bony prominences

distinguishingFeatures: More widespread synostoses including long bones

redFlags: Progressive joint stiffness leading to severe functional impairment
Signs of nerve compression such as numbness or weakness
Rapid onset of joint swelling or pain suggesting secondary complications
references: Spranger JW, et al. Bone Dysplasias: An Atlas of Genetic Disorders of Skeletal Development. 2002.
Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) entry for related synostosis syndromes
